variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, NP_000220.1:p.(Val246Phe). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; the review does not name the original publication in the row, so the person-level data are second-hand.
Zygosity, phase and family data are not given in the review; the batch row records zygosity as not reported.
Only one LCAT variant listed per person for a recessive disease; zygosity not stated.
Relationship between the two carriers not reported; they could be relatives from one family.
notes_for_panel: Two unclassified Dutch males (author Holleboom) each listed with c.736G>T only, zygosity not stated. Whether they are related is not reported. The review's reference list contains Holleboom et al. 2011, 'High Prevalence of Mutations in LCAT in Patients with Low HDL Cholesterol Levels in The Netherlands', a possible source, but the rows do not cite it.
